item.text:
**4B.4 Research Note**
Overall reading: strongly negative. I found no credible 2024 evidence that Erdoğan strengthened institutions that constrained him. The best counterevidence is narrow residual judicial resistance, but it was not reinforced by the executive and was often ignored.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak positive / counterevidence | [World Report 2024: Türkiye](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey | HRW notes that the Constitutional Court ordered Can Atalay released and later declared the parliamentary stripping of his mandate null and void. This shows some judicial resistance to executive pressure, but the same report says those rulings were ignored, so this is evidence of residual independence rather than Erdoğan strengthening the court. | 4B.4; 4B.1 |
| Negative | [Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says Erdoğan controls executive functions, exerts effective control over the legislature through the AKP, and frequently intervenes against ministries and independent public bodies that defy his wishes. That is direct evidence against strengthening legislative or oversight constraints. | 4B.4; 4B.1; 4B.2 |
| Negative | [World Report 2024: Türkiye](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey | HRW says the election campaign gave the ruling coalition an unjustified advantage, with TRT clearly favoring ruling parties and RTÜK issuing arbitrary fines to critical channels. That undercuts independent oversight of the media environment and shows state institutions being used to shield incumbency. | 4B.4; 4B.2; 4B.3 |
| Negative | [Türkiye: Kurdish Politicians Convicted in Unjust Mass Trial](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/16/turkiye-kurdish-politicians-convicted-unjust-mass-trial) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-16 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/16/turkiye-kurdish-politicians-convicted-unjust-mass-trial | HRW says the conviction of 24 Kurdish politicians was manifestly political and that the court ignored European Court of Human Rights rulings. This is evidence against an independent judiciary willing to constrain the ruler. | 4B.4; 4B.1; 4B.2 |
| Negative | [Türkiye: Stonewalling on Charges for Officials in Earthquake Deaths](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/27/turkiye-stonewalling-charges-officials-earthquake-deaths) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-27 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/27/turkiye-stonewalling-charges-officials-earthquake-deaths | HRW says administrative permission rules and weak judicial scrutiny prevent meaningful accountability for officials tied to earthquake deaths. That is direct evidence against strengthening audit, oversight, or accountability mechanisms. | 4B.4; 3B.4 |
| Negative | [Turkey removes two more pro-Kurdish mayors from office for links to banned group](https://apnews.com/article/3c6c33fd7fa2d86c9dc34089e6a98c9b) | Associated Press | 2024-11-22 | https://apnews.com/article/3c6c33fd7fa2d86c9dc34089e6a98c9b | AP reports that elected mayors were removed and replaced with state appointees after opposition victories, with critics calling the moves politically motivated. This is strong evidence against strengthening local governments when they become politically inconvenient. | 4B.4; 4B.1; 4B.3 |

**Search gap**
I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Erdoğan strengthened parliament, the audit state, local autonomy, or judicial independence in ways that limited his own power. The evidence instead shows capture, pressure, and non-implementation of adverse rulings. The only real counterevidence is isolated judicial resistance, and even that was not backed by the executive.
